name: evutil sockaddr string parsing (IPv4/IPv6 + port)
description:
evutil_parse_sockaddr_port() is libevent's text-to-sockaddr parser: it takes an untrusted, attacker-controlled string (e.g. "ipv4:port", "[ipv6]:port", "ipv6%zone") and turns it into a binary struct sockaddr_in/sockaddr_in6, driving a hand-rolled bracket/colon splitter, a fixed 128-byte stack buffer copy of the address part, atoi-based port parsing, and the internal IPv4/IPv6 text-address decoders (evutil_inet_pton / evutil_inet_pton_scope, including the internal fallback IPv6 parser with its gap(::)/word-count/memmove logic when inet_pton is unavailable or USE_INTERNAL_PTON forces it). Because it is reachable straight from a raw string with no prior validation, out-of-bounds length math, zone-id/if_nametoindex handling, and the manual IPv6 word array handling are prime fuzz targets.
- evutil_parse_sockaddr_port: target; splits "[addr]:port" / "addr:port" / "addr" forms, copies the address substring into a 128-byte stack buffer (bounds-checked by len>sizeof(buf)-1), parses the port with atoi and range-checks 1..65535, then dispatches to the IPv4 or IPv6 pton path and copies the resulting sockaddr into the caller's buffer only if it fits *outlen.
- evutil_inet_pton: sibling/core; address-family dispatcher invoked both directly by the target and via evutil_inet_pton_scope; for AF_INET uses sscanf "%u.%u.%u.%u%c" with per-octet range checks, for AF_INET6 (when EVENT__HAVE_INET_PTON is absent or USE_INTERNAL_PTON is defined) implements a manual colon/hex-word tokenizer with "::" gap handling, word-count validation, and memmove-based gap compaction — this is the core state machine most likely to have off-by-one/parsing bugs.
- evutil_inet_pton_scope: core/variant; same entry class as evutil_parse_sockaddr_port's AF_INET6 path but exposed publicly ("public for unit tests"); extracts a "%zone" suffix, resolves it via if_nametoindex() or strtoul() fallback, strdups the address part (mm_strdup/mm_free) and forwards to evutil_inet_pton — adds the zone-id parsing input path not reachable through the plain parse_sockaddr_port when no '%' is present, but is the same function parse_sockaddr_port calls for sin6.
- evutil_format_sockaddr_port_: consumer; takes the sockaddr produced by the target and serializes it back with evutil_inet_ntop into "addr:port" / "[addr]:port" text, giving a natural round-trip (parse -> format) the harness can exercise; internal-only (no EVENT2_EXPORT_SYMBOL) but linked in the same translation unit and used by libevent's own regress_util tests right after parsing.
- evutil_inet_ntop: inverse/consumer helper used by evutil_format_sockaddr_port_ to turn the parsed binary address back to text, exercising the printable-address encoding paths for both AF_INET and AF_INET6.
Input space: address family is selected implicitly by string shape — leading '[' forces IPv6; a second ':' after the first colon implies IPv6 without brackets; a single ':' implies IPv4:port; no ':' means bare address. Within IPv6 parsing, branches include embedded IPv4-in-IPv6 tail ("::ffff:1.2.3.4"), the "::" zero-run compression (gapPos handling, setWords count 0..8), presence/absence of a "%zone" scope suffix (interface name vs numeric index via if_nametoindex/strtoul), and whether EVENT__HAVE_INET_PTON/USE_INTERNAL_PTON select the OS inet_pton or libevent's internal hand-rolled decoder. Port text can be absent, zero, negative, >65535 (all rejected) or valid 1-65535. Address-part length can exceed the internal 128-byte stack buffer (rejected with -1) or fit.
Input format: evutil_parse_sockaddr_port takes a plain NUL-terminated C string, no binary header/magic — for utils_fuzzer the harness should treat the fuzz bytes as that string (ensuring NUL termination), covering forms like "1.2.3.4", "1.2.3.4:80", "::1", "[::1]:80", "fe80::1%eth0", and malformed/truncated variants (unterminated '[', missing ']', empty address, oversized address). No special byte-compatible seed corpus/dictionary files were found for this target beyond libevent's own regress_util.c test table, which is a good source of valid/invalid example strings.
Init rejections: the function rejects strings whose bracketed address substring is longer than 127 bytes, ports <=0 or >65535, '[' without a matching ']', any address that evutil_inet_pton/evutil_inet_pton_scope cannot parse (bad octet ranges, malformed hex groups, wrong word count, double "::"), and results that don't fit in the caller's *outlen — there is no strict/lax mode switch to relax these, they are the only acceptance path.
Structured input: not a language/grammar; valid example address/port strings are enumerated in test/regress_util.c (sa_port_ents, sa_pred_entries tables) and can seed the fuzz corpus.
Test hooks/debug switches: none found specific to this feature (no allocation-failure injection or SIMD toggles apply here); evutil_inet_pton_scope's choice between inet_pton vs. the internal parser is a compile-time macro (USE_INTERNAL_PTON / EVENT__HAVE_INET_PTON), not a runtime switch, so both can't be forced from the fuzzer but the internal parser is already exercised on platforms that enable it.
